deep.reconstruction:
This slip is not a Ramanujan derivation. It is a referee's or editor's cover note, probably in the hand of G. N. Watson or G. H. Hardy, attached to the manuscript catalogued as Add. Ms. a94^18 (16). The next page states that manuscript's theorems on the Diophantine approximation of e^{2/a}. For integer a, Ramanujan claims liminf (and the matching lower bound) of the distance of N e^{2/a} from the integer below or above it is ~ log log N / (|a| N log N), with constant 1/(4|a|) in case III (odd a, distance to the next integer).

Step 1, the critique. The annotator finds the manuscript 'apparently very incomplete'. A struck-out remark reads '(Does (6) follow from text ...)'. In pencil, the annotator asks whether (10) is justified, 'what diff does |a| (transcribed |c|) make?', and questions (13) and (14). These presumably refer to the numbered steps of Ramanujan's proof, which are not on this page.

Step 2, the parity check. Write v_n for the sequence used in the proof. This is presumably the numerators or denominators of the continued-fraction convergents of e^{2/a}, satisfying v_{n+1} = c_{n+1} v_n + v_{n-1}. That identification is my reconstruction, not stated on the page. On this reading v_{n+1} - v_{n-1} = c_{n+1} v_n, so the parity of v_{n+1} follows from those of v_{n-1} and of c_{n+1} v_n. The annotator works three cases:
- v_3 - v_1 even and v_1 odd, so v_3 is odd.
- v_4 - v_2 odd and v_2 even, so v_4 is odd.
- v_5 - v_3 odd and v_3 odd, so v_5 is even, with a query mark.

The parity of the convergent denominators matters because it decides on which side of an integer N e^{2/a} falls. That is exactly what separates the 'fractional part small' cases (I) from the 'distance to next integer small' cases (II, III). It also explains why odd a gives the extra factor 1/4.

For odd a = k, Euler's expansion is e^{2/k} = [1; (k-1)/2, 6k, (5k-1)/2, 1, 1, (7k-1)/2, 18k, (11k-1)/2, 1, 1, ...]. For even a the partial quotients include non-integers, so the expansion must be rescaled. This is plausibly the source of the '|a|' and parity questions.
errors: The parity arithmetic on the page is internally correct: even+odd=odd, odd+even=odd, odd+odd=even. The query on 'v_5 even?' signals doubt about whether the premises (the parities of v_5 - v_3) hold, not an arithmetic slip.
The steps (6), (10), (13), (14) being criticised are not on this page, so their correctness cannot be judged here.
The previous page's v_n (numerical values approaching 1/(6*sqrt(3))) appear to belong to a different investigation and are not the v_n of this note.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an editorial or referee annotation, not Ramanujan's own mathematics. The underlying manuscript on approximating e^{2/a} is already known and discussed in the literature (Berndt-Kim-Zaharescu). The parity check is elementary.

transcription_corrections: 'with Add Ms a 94^18 (16)': the first word is the abbreviation 'wth' (with), written with an underlined superscript.
'what diff does |c| make?' should most likely read '|a|', matching the |a| in the theorems on the next page.
The struck-out parenthesis reads roughly '(Does (6) follow from text ...)'; the last word is illegible and 'test zz' is doubtful.
The lines '(10)? & what diff does |a| make?' and '(13) & (14) ?' are in faint pencil. The rest of the note, including the v-parity table, is in ink.
The handwriting is not Ramanujan's; it is likely an editor's or referee's (Watson or Hardy).
